cases.label: distinct
cases.text: The tally starts at 19. The clerk posted a 4-point addition for parcel PINE. The copy shows a 4-point addition for BIRCH, a separate parcel the clerk also posted. Finally multiply the tally by 3.
cases.note: Both parcels received their own posting.

cases.label: outside
cases.text: Start with 32 points. Add 5 for the relay. The relay route was 5 miles long. Finally multiply the points by 2.
cases.note: The second numeral measures distance.

cases.label: same
cases.text: The game starts at 30 points. A scorer applied -5 for the missed gate. The umpire's -5 for the missed gate was a written copy of that ruling. Multiply the final score by 2.
cases.note: The umpire copied the first deduction.

cases.label: uncertain
cases.text: Begin with 13 credits. On Monday, six credits were added for a desk move. Tuesday's log says six credits for the desk move; nobody knows whether the crew moved it again or the clerk copied Monday's entry. Multiply the resulting balance by 4.
cases.note: The later entry could be a copy or a second move.

cases.label: same
cases.text: Opening balance: 28 tickets. Refund RAVEN added 7 tickets. In other words, that refund put 7 tickets back. Multiply the balance by 3 at the end.
cases.note: The prose restates the named refund.

cases.label: uncertain
cases.text: The tally starts at 19. The clerk posted a 4-point addition for parcel PINE. The copy shows a 4-point addition with a torn parcel label; even the clerk cannot tell whether it was a reprint or another parcel. Finally multiply the tally by 3.
cases.note: The label that would distinguish a new parcel from a reprint is unreadable.

cases.label: outside
cases.text: The counter starts at 24. A weigh-in added 6 points. Then multiply the counter by 6.
cases.note: The repeated number is the multiplier.

cases.label: distinct
cases.text: The game starts at 30 points. A scorer applied -5 for the missed gate. The umpire applied -5 for the false start as well. Multiply the final score by 2.
cases.note: The scorer and umpire imposed penalties for different infractions.

cases.label: same
cases.text: Begin with 13 credits. On Monday, six credits were added for a desk move. Tuesday's log says six credits for the desk move; the clerk copied Monday's entry into Tuesday's log. Multiply the resulting balance by 4.
cases.note: Tuesday is the date of copying, not of a second move.

cases.label: uncertain
cases.text: The inventory starts at 18 crates. The morning pickup added 2 crates. The evening pickup would have added 2 crates if the driver showed up; no one knows if she did. Finally multiply the crate count by 5.
cases.note: The evening pickup was conditional and its completion is unknown.

cases.label: distinct
cases.text: The account starts with 26 tokens. Inez returned a jar and added 8 tokens to the account for that return. Later she returned a second jar and added 8 tokens for it. Multiply the final balance by 3.
cases.note: Each return earned tokens, even though Inez made both.

cases.label: outside
cases.text: Start with 17 tokens. Add 3 for the book return. A sign on the wall reads '3 for a postcard'. Finally multiply the token balance by 2.
cases.note: The quoted number is a posted price.

cases.label: uncertain
cases.text: The game starts at 30 points. A scorer applied -5 for the missed gate. The umpire proposed -5 for the false start; that ruling is still pending. Multiply the final score by 2.
cases.note: The second penalty has been proposed but has no final ruling.

cases.label: same
cases.text: The tally starts at 19. The clerk posted a 4-point addition for parcel PINE. The copy shows a 4-point addition for PINE, a reprint of the original posting. Finally multiply the tally by 3.
cases.note: The copy identifies the same parcel posting.

cases.label: outside
cases.text: Start the board at 31. Add 4 points for the quiz. The prize requires a score ending in 4. Multiply the board total by 3.
cases.note: The last digit of a qualifying score is not an amount added to the board.

cases.label: distinct
cases.text: Begin with 13 credits. On Monday, six credits were added for a desk move. Tuesday's log says six credits for the desk move; the crew earned them by moving the desk again on Tuesday. Multiply the resulting balance by 4.
cases.note: The crew earned another addition for a second move.

cases.label: same
cases.text: The board starts at 25 points. The referee subtracted three for the late pass. Her report put the late-pass deduction at three. Then multiply the board total by 4.
cases.note: The report gives the size of the referee's deduction.

cases.label: distinct
cases.text: Start with 42 points. A red flag cost 4 points. A separate blue flag also cost 4 points. Multiply what remains by 3.
cases.note: Both flag penalties were assessed.

cases.label: uncertain
cases.text: The till starts with 37 coins. The fruit stall paid in 5 coins for its permit. A loose slip says 'flower stall: 5 coins due'; the slip does not say whether the stall ever paid. Finally multiply the till balance by 2.
cases.note: The second fee was due but its payment is unknown.

cases.label: outside
cases.text: Begin with 8 stamps. Add 8 stamps from the harbor booth. Finally multiply the number of stamps by 3.
cases.note: One numeral is the opening balance.

cases.label: same
cases.text: Start at 14 points. Bea earned 5 for sorting the maps. 'Map duty: 5 earned,' read Bea's copy of that award. Then multiply the score by 2.
cases.note: Bea's copy names the same map-sorting award.

cases.label: uncertain
cases.text: The score starts at 23. The judge added 7 for Nia's vault. The scoreboard also shows 7 under 'floor'; the judge is checking whether the vault award was copied there or a floor award was made. Finally multiply the score by 3.
cases.note: The displayed floor amount may be a new award or a copy of the vault award.

cases.label: distinct
cases.text: Opening count: 20. Posted: 6 added for unloading the van. Also posted: 6 added for packing the crates. Final step: multiply the count by 2.
cases.note: The ledger posts a separate addition for each job.

cases.label: outside
cases.text: Start the day with 11 points. Add 2 points for a ride on bus number 2. Multiply the final score by 4.
cases.note: The bus number is an identifier, not a second award.

boundaries.text: Start with 20 credits. Iris requested a rebate of 6 credits. The supervisor approved a rebate of 6 credits, but the payment record says the rebate was only partly paid and omits the amount. Add the credits Iris actually received, then multiply the result by 2.
boundaries.note: Request and approval both specify 6. The partial payment has no stated amount.

boundaries.text: Start with 9 seals in the north cupboard. The south cupboard received a delivery of 4 seals. The west cupboard also received a delivery of 4 seals. The line giving the size of the north cupboard's delivery is torn off. Add the north cupboard's delivery and then multiply by 3.
boundaries.note: Both quantities belong to deliveries to other cupboards. Neither determines the north delivery.

boundaries.text: Start with 12 tickets. Monday's ticket release added 5 tickets. Friday's ticket release added 5 tickets. Add the tickets from Thursday's release to the starting count and multiply the result by 4. The Thursday bulletin gives only the time of the release.
boundaries.note: The two counts of 5 refer to different days. Thursday's release size is missing.

boundaries.text: Start with 11 parcels. The delivery docket records 7 crates. The depot's scale records 7 kilograms for that delivery. Add the number of individual parcels in the delivery, then multiply by 2. Several parcels can share a crate, and their weights vary.
boundaries.note: Neither the crate count nor the weight specifies the parcel count, even though the delivery is the same.

boundaries.text: Start with 14 points. The draft cited a 'bonus of 8 points'. The correction says the bonus of 8 points was a sample entry copied from the handbook. Add the bonus actually awarded and then multiply by 3. The correction confirms an award but leaves its amount blank.
boundaries.note: Both mentions of 8 are traceable to one rejected example. The real award is unquantified.

boundaries.text: Start with the opening balance of 8 credits. The shift sheet also shows 8 credits per hour. Add the credits earned during the shift and multiply the updated balance by 5. The hours worked are missing from the shift sheet.
boundaries.note: An opening balance and an hourly rate do not determine the shift earnings without the hours.

boundaries.text: Start with 8 seals in the east cupboard. The delivery docket records 4 seals for the east cupboard. The receiving clerk copied that docket into the log as 'delivery of 4 seals to the east cupboard'. Add the seals received, then multiply the updated count by 3.
boundaries.note: The clerk copied the original docket. One delivery raises 8 to 12, then multiplication gives 36.

boundaries.text: Start with 12 tickets. Thursday's release added 5 tickets. On Friday the office published a recap of Thursday's release and listed the 5 tickets again. Add the tickets released on Thursday to the starting count, then multiply by 4.
boundaries.note: Friday is the publication date of a recap. Both mentions describe Thursday's single release.

boundaries.text: Start with 14 points. The award letter grants a bonus of 8 points. The corrected award letter still grants 8 points and fixes the spelling of the recipient's name. Add the awarded bonus and then multiply by 3.
boundaries.note: The name correction preserves the single award. Adding 8 once and tripling gives 66.

post_trial.text: The game starts at 30 points. A scorer proposed -5 for the missed gate. The umpire's -5 for the missed gate was a written copy of that ruling. The ruling is still pending. Multiply the final score by 2.
The game starts at 30 points. A scorer applied -5 for the missed gate. The umpire applied a separate -5 for the missed gate on the next lap. Multiply the final score by 2.
The game starts at 30 points. A scorer deducted 5 for the missed gate. The umpire's 5 for the missed gate was a written copy of that deduction. Multiply the final score by 2.

The game starts at 30 points. A scorer recorded but never applied -5 for the missed gate. The umpire's -5 for the missed gate was a written copy of that proposed ruling. Multiply the final score by 2.
